title: byok: omit store for custom Responses endpoints
body:
## Summary

- Omits `store` from Custom Endpoint Responses requests when `zeroDataRetentionEnabled` is not configured, allowing each implementation to apply its own default.
- Keeps explicitly enabled zero data retention requests stateless by sending `store: false` and not reusing `previous_response_id`.
- Preserves ordinary OpenAI BYOK behavior and Custom Endpoint request shaping after context-size cloning.

Fixes #331636

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Custom Endpoint Responses models share the OpenAI-compatible endpoint implementation. That implementation coerced the optional zero data retention flag to a boolean and assigned `store` from the result, so an omitted flag became `store: true`. Custom Responses implementations can rely on the property being absent and applying their own retention default, particularly when continuing a tool-calling turn.

### Implementation

The Custom Endpoint endpoint now removes `store` only for Responses requests whose zero data retention setting is undefined. Explicitly enabled zero data retention continues through the shared path, which sends `store: false` and disables stateful marker reuse. The Custom Endpoint clone path preserves the concrete endpoint type so context-size overrides do not discard this request shaping.

### Behavior and constraints

- Chat Completions and Messages requests are unchanged.
- Explicit `zeroDataRetentionEnabled: false` retains the existing `store: true` behavior.
- Ordinary OpenAI BYOK endpoints retain their existing Responses behavior.
- Stateful `previous_response_id` reuse remains enabled only when retention permits it.

### Review context

The main compatibility boundary is the tri-state configuration: omitted, explicitly enabled, and explicitly disabled must remain distinct for Custom Endpoint models while other providers keep their current behavior.

</details>

title: Run UI validation scenarios without configuring an MCP server
body:
Stacked on #331674: this PR targets that branch, so the diff below is only the runner. It will retarget to `main` automatically once #331674 merges.

## Why

The `ui-scenario-validation` skill could only be used by first registering `test/mcp` as an MCP server and then driving `vscode_automation_evidence_start` / `_step` / `_finish` by hand. That is a lot of setup for a one-off reproduction, and it puts the capability out of reach of a plain request like *"reproduce this issue against Insiders and record it"*.

## What

`runScenario` takes a scenario file and runs it end to end:

```bash
node test/mcp/out/runScenario.js <scenario.js> --build "<app-root>"
```

A scenario is plain JavaScript — kept outside the repository, next to the run it produces:

```js
module.exports = {
	id: 'vscode-250159-settings-search',
	title: 'Settings search matches across title and description',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159',
	workspacePath,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'SS-01',
			title: 'Open the Settings editor',
			async run(context) {
				await context.workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('workbench.action.openSettings2');
				await context.page.waitForSelector('.settings-editor', { state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
				return 'The Settings editor is visible.';
			}
		}
	]
};
```

Each step receives the `Application`, the `Workbench` helpers and the Playwright `Page`. It returns a string describing how it was validated, throws to fail, or calls `skip(reason)` when a precondition is unavailable.

The runner launches VS Code with video and tracing, captures a screenshot at every step boundary, stops at the first failed or skipped step, writes `report.html`, and renders the chapter titles onto the recording. Clean capture is on by default, so the recording shows unmodified UI and titles are added afterwards.

**A skipped step reports the run as `aborted`, not `passed`** — the scenario did not validate, and reporting a pass would overstate the result. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed or aborted, `2` usage.

The skill is rewritten around this flow. The MCP server stays available for interactive exploration, where inspecting the UI before choosing an assertion is worth the setup.

## Verification

The example in `SKILL.md` was extracted from the file programmatically and run verbatim against installed Insiders, so the documented API is executed rather than assumed:

```
Evidence run: .../vscode-250159-settings-search-2026-08-19T18-14-49-151Z
  PASS SS-01 Open the Settings editor
  FAIL SS-02 Search across title and description: Max Requests is absent. Found: Confirm Edit Request Removal, ...
Report: .../report.html
Rendered 2 step chapters into videos/annotated.mp4
Outcome: failed
```

That failure is the point: it reproduces [#250159](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159). Also verified:

- `skip()` stops the run, leaves later steps unexecuted, and reports `aborted`
- malformed scenarios (missing `id`, duplicate step ids, missing `run`) fail before VS Code launches
- the dev-build path still launches and finishes
- the annotated video contains the step cards and the real, unmodified workbench

## Note on the example

The first draft of the documented example asserted that a setting was **absent** without scrolling the settings tree. That tree is virtualized, so it renders only the rows near the viewport — the assertion would have been satisfied by a setting merely being below the fold. The example now scrolls the whole list, and the skill calls this trap out explicitly.

title: Add local timestamps to Copilot Chat diagnostics files for improved traceability

body:
## Description
When troubleshooting issues with GitHub Copilot Chat in VS Code, exporting or collecting multiple diagnostic files lacks chronological metadata. This makes it difficult to correlate events across multiple diagnostic runs and establish a clear timeline of chat-related issues.

## Problem
Currently, the Copilot Chat diagnostics feature generates diagnostic files and output without timestamps in:
- **Filenames**: Generated diagnostic files have UUIDs or generic names but lack temporal information
- **File contents**: Diagnostic reports don't include when diagnostics were collected or when individual events occurred
- **Debug logs**: Individual event logs lack precise timestamps for correlation across multiple exports

When debugging multiple Copilot Chat issues over time, users must manually track when each diagnostic was collected, leading to:
- Difficulty correlating events across multiple diagnostic exports
- Loss of chronological context when files are moved or shared
- Inefficient troubleshooting workflows with unclear timelines
- Inability to match Chat events with system logs or other diagnostics that have timestamps

## Solution
Add ISO 8601 local timestamps throughout the Chat diagnostics system:

1. **Filename Timestamps**: Include ISO 8601 timestamp in diagnostic export filenames
   - Example: `copilot-chat-diagnostics-2026-08-19T14-30-45Z.json`
   - Enables quick visual identification of when diagnostics were collected

2. **Report Header Timestamps**: Add timestamp metadata to diagnostics report
   - Collection start time and completion time
   - Local timezone for user context
   - Reporter user info and session identifiers

3. **Per-Event Timestamps**: Add precise timestamps for individual chat events
   - Message send/receive times
   - Tool execution start/end times
   - Permission/approval event times
   - Debug log entry times

## Related Code Files
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/log/vscode-node/loggingActions.ts` - Diagnostics collection and formatting
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatDebug/agentHostUsageSidecar.ts` - Reference implementation with ISO timestamps
- `extensions/copilot/docs/monitoring/agent_monitoring_arch.md` - Monitoring and traceability documentation
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/vscode-node/tools/getDiagnostics.ts` - Diagnostics tool implementation

## Benefits
- ✅ Improved traceability when troubleshooting Chat connectivity and functionality issues
- ✅ Better correlation of events across multiple diagnostic exports
- ✅ Easier timeline reconstruction for debugging complex Chat issues
- ✅ Enhanced ability to match Chat diagnostics with system logs (which already have timestamps)
- ✅ Clearer understanding of when issues occurred and their sequence
- ✅ More professional diagnostic reports with complete temporal context
- ✅ Better support experience for development and support teams

## Example Impact
**Before**: "I have 5 Copilot Chat diagnostic exports - which one captured the issue I'm debugging?"
**After**: "The diagnostic from 2026-08-19T14:30:45Z shows the exact failure point with clear event sequence"

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All Copilot Chat diagnostic export files include ISO 8601 timestamp in filename
- [ ] Diagnostic report header includes collection start/end times and timezone
- [ ] All individual events in diagnostic logs include precise timestamps
- [ ] Timestamps work correctly across different timezones and locales
- [ ] Timestamps are preserved when diagnostic files are shared or moved
- [ ] Documentation updated to explain timestamp format and usage

title: markdown: fix: correlate forwarded undo/redo restores
body:
Companion to microsoft/vscode-packages#279 (`markdown-editor: fix: correlate forwarded history restores`).

## Problem

The Markdown custom editor does not own its undo stack — the backing `TextDocument` does — so undo/redo chords in the webview are forwarded to the extension host, which runs the built-in `undo`/`redo` command. That forwarding was fire-and-forget:

- The webview never learned whether the command actually restored anything, so it could not attribute a restore to the chord or reveal the restored caret.
- Restored content arrived only via the generic `update` message, which carried no version, so a slow or reordered message could apply superseded text.
- A failed command silently did nothing.

`@vscode/markdown-editor` is gaining an asynchronous history strategy whose `undo`/`redo` return `PromiseLike<{kind:'unchanged'} | {kind:'restored', state}>`, with the controller revalidating the returned state before its reveal. This PR is the host half of that contract.

## The handshake

```
webview   --> { type: 'history', command, requestId }
extension --> { type: 'historyResult', requestId, status: 'restored' | 'unchanged' | 'failed', ... }
```

`restored` also carries `content` and `documentVersion`. Ordinary `update` messages now carry `documentVersion` too.

## Webview (`markdown-editor-src/editor.ts`)

- Each chord gets a monotonically increasing `requestId`; the pending `resolve`/`reject` pair is tracked and settled by the matching result. On dispose, in-flight requests resolve as `unchanged` so controller continuations cannot run against a torn-down editor.
- `#lastDocumentVersion` tracks the host revision whose content was last applied; `update` messages and history results with an older version are ignored. Messages without a version are still accepted, so an older host keeps working.
- A `restored` result applies the authoritative content via `replaceSourceText` (which maps the selection through the change and clears stale pending-paragraph state), captures the exact resulting `sourceText`/`selection`, and resolves `{kind:'restored', state}`. A no-op resolves `{kind:'unchanged'}`; a `failed` result rejects.
- `onError` logs the rejection and deliberately posts nothing, so a broken request cannot start another protocol round trip.

## Extension (`src/preview/markdownEditorProvider.ts`)

1. Drain `editQueue` so the chord cannot race a pending edit.
2. If the panel is not active, reply `unchanged` — the command would land on a different document.
3. Snapshot `document.version` immediately before the built-in command, await it, then capture version and content immediately after.
4. Reply via the pure helper `historyResultPayload`: `restored` (with content and the new version) only when the command changed `document.version`, otherwise `unchanged`. A rejection is traced and replied to as `failed` with a safe, non-leaking message.

All ordinary `update` posts now include `documentVersion`.

## Intentional cross-version source compatibility

The history strategy is assigned to a local variable rather than written inline in the `EditorController` options. As an inline literal, the extra `asynchronous`/`onError` members would trip excess-property checking against the **currently published** synchronous `IHistoryStrategy`. As a variable, the object stays assignable to the current interface (which ignores the extras and tolerates the promise as a `void` return) while the **forthcoming** package recognizes it as an `IAsynchronousHistoryStrategy`. No future-only types are imported; the result shape is mirrored with local declarations, so CI against the published package is unaffected.

## Validation

- Type-checked `markdown-editor-src` against **both** the published and the forthcoming package type definitions; both pass. A probe confirmed the future-only type is genuinely absent from the published package, i.e. the compatibility concern is real rather than theoretical.
- New focused unit test for `historyResultPayload` covering no-op vs. restored attribution.
- `npm run build-markdown-editor`, `tsc --noEmit` for the extension, and ESLint over both changed source trees.

No dependency, lockfile, or generated `package.json` contribution changes are included; the local package link used for verification was removed.

## Risks

- Until the new package ships, the returned promise is ignored by the published controller, so behavior there is unchanged; the correlated reveal activates with the package upgrade.
- The stale-version guard assumes monotonic `TextDocument.version`, which holds.
- Panel-inactive chords now reply `unchanged` rather than being silently dropped — this is the intended causal attribution, not a regression.

title: Make UI scenario validation work against an installed build, without an MCP server
body:
The `ui-scenario-validation` skill documents running a scenario against an installed build, and driving it through the `test/mcp` MCP server. Neither worked as documented: the installed-build path could not launch at all, and the MCP requirement put the skill out of reach of a plain request.

## `VSCODE_DEV=1` was applied to `--build` runs

Launching against installed Insiders always failed with:

```
Failed to launch Electron within 60000ms.
Original error: electronApplication.waitForEvent: Timeout 60000ms exceeded while waiting for event "window"
```

The Electron environment is resolved once at module load, and correctly: `VSCODE_DEV`, `VSCODE_CLI` and `VSCODE_REPOSITORY` are only set when there is no `--build`. `getApplication` then re-applied the same block unconditionally, so every launch was marked as running from source. A packaged build that believes it is running from a checkout never opens a window, so Playwright waits for a `window` event that never arrives.

Bisected against installed Insiders, holding everything else constant:

| Environment | First window |
|---|---|
| clean | opens |
| `VSCODE_DEV=1` | **never opens** |
| `VSCODE_CLI=1` | opens |
| `VSCODE_REPOSITORY=<repo>` | opens |

`VSCODE_DEV` alone accounts for it. The duplicated block also re-derived and re-validated the dev Electron path, which is already validated at module load for whichever target is selected, so it is removed rather than made conditional.

## The installed extensions directory was used

No extensions directory was ever passed, so a `--build` run loaded whatever the user has installed. That contradicts the isolated-profile guarantee the skill relies on: third-party extensions change the product under test and their logs are copied into the evidence bundle.

A settings-search scenario recorded before this change shipped logs for GitLens, ESLint, Prettier, the .NET runtime extension and two internal extensions, and their contributed settings appeared in the result list being asserted on. After it, the only extension left is the one bundled with Insiders — part of the product under test.

The launcher now uses an isolated directory under the existing test data path, matching what `test/smoke/src/main.ts` already does.

Per-run `extraArgs` are appended *after* the generated arguments, and `argv.ts` resolves a repeated string option with `val.pop() // take the last`, so a caller could have handed back the real directory. A shared `assertNoProfileOverrides` helper now rejects `--user-data-dir` and `--extensions-dir` (both `--opt value` and `--opt=value`) on the launch path *and* the restart tool, which previously had no guard at all.

## A stable build was downloaded on every run and never used

`setup` downloaded the previous stable release on every `--build` launch. The test data directory it downloads into is wiped at startup, so this was not a one-time cost: **335 MB and about 36 seconds on every run**, before VS Code even started.

The downloaded path was only ever assigned to `opts['stable-build']`, which nothing in this server reads — migration tests belong to the smoke test runner, which has its own copy of this logic. Removed, along with the now-unused `--stable-build` option.

## Running a scenario no longer needs an MCP server

The skill could only be used by first registering `test/mcp` as an MCP server and then driving `vscode_automation_evidence_start` / `_step` / `_finish` by hand. `runScenario` takes a scenario file and runs it end to end instead:

```bash
node test/mcp/out/runScenario.js <scenario.js> --build "<app-root>"
```

A scenario is plain JavaScript, kept outside the repository next to the run it produces:

```js
module.exports = {
	id: 'vscode-250159-settings-search',
	title: 'Settings search matches across title and description',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159',
	workspacePath,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'SS-01',
			title: 'Open the Settings editor',
			async run(context) {
				await context.workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('workbench.action.openSettings2');
				await context.page.waitForSelector('.settings-editor', { state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
				return 'The Settings editor is visible.';
			}
		}
	]
};
```

Each step receives the `Application`, the `Workbench` helpers and the Playwright `Page`. It returns a string describing how it was validated, throws to fail, or calls `skip(reason)` when a precondition is unavailable.

The runner launches VS Code with video and tracing, captures a screenshot at every step boundary, stops at the first failed or skipped step, writes `report.html`, and renders the chapter titles onto the recording. Clean capture is on by default, so the recording shows unmodified UI and the titles are added afterwards.

**A skipped step reports the run as `aborted`, not `passed`** — the scenario did not validate, and reporting a pass would overstate the result. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed or aborted, `2` usage.

The skill is renamed to `validate-ui-scenario` and rewritten around this flow. Workspace skills are surfaced as slash commands named after the skill, so the name is what a user types: `/validate-ui-scenario reproduce <issue url> against my installed Insiders`. The MCP server remains available for interactive exploration, where inspecting the UI before choosing an assertion is worth the setup.

## The recording is captioned, not chaptered

Step titles were shown on full-screen cards spliced between segments. That stretched the timeline, and it told the viewer nothing about what the step actually *checked* — the validation detail was meant to appear on those cards but never did, because it was read from the opening capture, which only records that a step started. The field was always empty.

The band is drawn above the frame instead: `pad` grows the canvas and `drawtext` writes into the added strip, timed with `enable='between(t,...)'`. The recording keeps its original length, and **no recorded pixel is covered** — the status bar and the bottom of the workbench stay readable. Each caption carries the step number and id, its status, the title, and the validation detail from the closing capture, coloured green, red or amber; the run outcome sits in the corner for the whole video.

This also collapses the render to a single ffmpeg pass; the previous version trimmed a segment per step, generated a card per step, and concatenated them.

Verified on a real run — the captions track the UI state, not just the arithmetic: during `SS-01` the settings search box is empty, and it contains `chat confirm` during `SS-02`. Also checked with synthetic manifests: a detail containing `100%` renders (drawtext expansion stays off), over-long titles and details wrap and then truncate rather than overflowing, a skipped step shows amber with no detail line, and a missing ffmpeg still exits 0 with a warning.

## Scenario files need a `.cjs` extension

This package is an ES module package, so a CommonJS scenario saved as `.js` inside the repository is treated as ESM and fails to load — which is exactly what the skill told people to do. My own verification missed it because I had been running scenarios from outside the repository. The skill now says `.cjs`, and an ES module scenario with a default export works as well.
## Verification

Everything below was exercised on Windows against installed Insiders 1.135.0-insider and against a dev build from source.

The example in `SKILL.md` was extracted from the file programmatically and run verbatim, so the documented API is executed rather than assumed:

```

  FAIL SS-02 Search across title and description: Max Requests is absent. Found: Confirm Edit Request Removal, ...
Report: .../report.html
Rendered 2 step chapters into videos/annotated.mp4
Outcome: failed
```

That failure is the point: it reproduces [#250159](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159) — searching `chat confirm` in the Settings editor does not match `Max Requests`, while `max requests` does. Also verified:

- installed Insiders via `--build`: fails to launch before this change, records a full run after
- the dev build path is unchanged, and still launches and finishes
- `skip()` stops the run, leaves later steps unexecuted, and reports `aborted`
- malformed scenarios (missing `id`, duplicate step ids, missing `run`) fail before VS Code launches
- the annotated video contains the step cards and the real, unmodified workbench
- a full `--build` evidence run drops from about 90s to 19s, with the first window arriving 173ms after launch

## Note on the example

The first draft of the documented example asserted that a setting was **absent** without scrolling the settings tree. That tree is virtualized, so it renders only the rows near the viewport — the assertion would have been satisfied by a setting merely being below the fold. The example now scrolls the whole list, and the skill calls this trap out explicitly.

## Summary

Electron 42.8.1 introduces a Windows renderer layout regression that materially slows VS Code startup. The regression remains in Electron 42.9.3.

The same VS Code application on Electron 42.8.1 is 50-87 ms slower than on 42.8.0 in repeated startup measurements. A minimal renderer benchmark isolates the change to forced Blink layout: 110.0 ms on 42.8.0 versus 145.2 ms on 42.8.1 (+32%). Equivalent JavaScript execution does not regress.

![Electron 42.8.1 Windows renderer layout regression](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a47a044f-ec49-4f69-a6d3-b4fc92dadae0)

## Impact on VS Code startup

This was found while analyzing Windows desktop startup performance across 154 published Insiders builds from July 1 through August 18.

Adjacent published build boundary:

| | Last known good | First known bad |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Commit | `f844934f854c9277a48627aac77ebcea69591ae1` | `68939d5cba5de82713a8b1bd8e34a10b44d465d5` |
| VS Code version | 1.134.0-insider | 1.134.0-insider |
| Electron | 42.8.0 | 42.8.1 |
| Chromium | 148.0.7778.271 | 148.0.7778.280 |
| V8 | 14.8.178.33-electron.0 | 14.8.178.38-electron.0 |
| Node.js | 24.17.0 | 24.18.1 |
| Median startup | 1364 ms | 1411 ms |

Measured regression:

- +47 ms (+3.45%)
- Bootstrap 95% interval: +36 ms to +61 ms
- The next published build remains at the first-bad level: -5 ms, interval -19 ms to +4 ms.

The source range contains `1fc102e9ae7264920fcc41986d7c4d8231f557f7`, `chore: bump electron@42.8.1` (#330244).

## Runtime/app partition

Reciprocal hybrid builds separate the runtime and VS Code application:

| Electron runtime | VS Code app | Median startup |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 42.8.0 | Last-good app | 1374 ms (A1), 1362 ms (A2) |
| 42.8.1 | Last-good app | 1419 ms |
| 42.8.0 | First-bad app | 1425 ms |
| 42.8.1 | First-bad app | 1425 ms |

The runtime-only hybrid reproduces a 45-57 ms increase. Product changes in the same published-build gap add overlapping critical-path cost, but do not explain the Electron-only result.

## Official Electron runtime comparison

The identical last-good VS Code app was grafted onto verified official Windows x64 Electron archives:

| Runtime | Median startup |
| --- | ---: |
| Electron 42.8.0 A1 | 1372 ms |
| Electron 42.8.1 | 1459 ms |
| Electron 42.9.3 | 1494 ms |
| Electron 42.8.0 A2 | 1409 ms |

Comparisons:

- 42.8.1 versus 42.8.0 A1: +87 ms (+6.34%), interval +75 ms to +111 ms
- 42.8.1 versus 42.8.0 A2: +50 ms (+3.55%), interval +28 ms to +73 ms
- 42.8.0 control drift: +37 ms, interval +28 ms to +58 ms
- 42.9.3 versus 42.8.1: +35 ms, comparable to control drift; 42.9.3 does not recover

Each batch used three warmups and fifteen measured starts. Execution was interleaved 42.8.0 / 42.8.1 / 42.9.3 / 42.8.0.

## Trace results

Trace categories:

```text
base,browser,content,loading,navigation,mojom,renderer_host,renderer,startup,toplevel,v8,blink,blink.user_timing,gpu,cc,disabled-by-default-v8.compile,disabled-by-default-v8.cpu_profiler,disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline,devtools.timeline
```

Two marked Chrome JSON startup traces per adjacent build were captured. Instrumented median:

- Renderer start to workbench ready: 1933.2 ms -> 2041.5 ms (+108.2 ms)

Largest renderer changes:

| Trace event | 42.8.0 | 42.8.1 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `RunTask` | 1481.1 ms | 1596.5 ms | +115.4 ms |
| `Receive mojo message` | 892.7 ms | 981.8 ms | +89.0 ms |
| Style/layout update | 158.3 ms | 192.9 ms | +34.7 ms |
| `UpdateLayoutTree` | 51.9 ms | 76.0 ms | +24.1 ms |
| `V8.CompileCode` | 462.6 ms | 486.3 ms | +23.7 ms |

Browser-process `RunTask` changes by only +5.2 ms. The regression is renderer-specific.

The VS Code `perfBaseline` worker moves from approximately 20 ms to 24 ms. Running the same Fibonacci computation under Electron-as-Node is instead 2.5% faster on 42.8.1, which further narrows the regression to the renderer rather than generic Node/V8 execution.

## Minimal renderer reproduction

A fresh hidden renderer performs:

1. Recursive Fibonacci computation
2. Dynamic function compilation
3. Creation of 1,000 inline elements
4. Forty alternating class changes followed by `offsetWidth` reads
5. Repeated warm Fibonacci computation

Median of 15 alternating runs:

| Electron | Cold JS | Compile | Forced layout | Warm JS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 42.8.0 | 1.2 ms | 11.7 ms | 110.0 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.8.1 | 1.2 ms | 12.6 ms | 145.2 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.9.3 | 1.1 ms | 12.8 ms | 143.5 ms | 6.5 ms |

The forced-layout workload is 32% slower beginning in 42.8.1 and remains regressed in 42.9.3. Cold and warm JavaScript are effectively unchanged.

Core workload:

```js
for (let index = 0; index < 1000; index++) {
	const element = document.createElement('span');
	element.textContent = `item-${index}`;
	target.appendChild(element);
}

const start = performance.now();
for (let index = 0; index < 40; index++) {
	target.className = index % 2 === 0 ? 'compact' : 'expanded';
	width += target.offsetWidth;
}
const duration = performance.now() - start;
```

## Upstream change suspects

Electron 42.8.1 includes:

- Node.js 24.18.1
- Chromium/V8 patch updates
- Updated PGO profiles, including `win-x64.pgo.txt`

Electron 42.9.0 updates PGO profiles again, but 42.9.3 remains regressed in the minimal forced-layout benchmark.

Release references:

- https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v42.8.1
- https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v42.9.3

## Host and scenario

- Windows x64, OS build 10.0.26200
- AMD EPYC 7763, 32 logical processors
- High performance power plan
- 128 GB RAM
- Official VS Code Insiders ZIP archives, SHA-256 verified
- Standard startup: deterministic local folder and one text file
- Extensions, updates, experiments, workspace trust, GPU, telemetry, and crash reporting disabled
- Primary statistic: median warm startup

VS Code arguments include:

```text
--skip-welcome
--skip-release-notes
--disable-updates
--disable-experiments
--disable-extensions
--disable-workspace-trust
--disable-gpu
--disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion
--disable-telemetry
--disable-crash-reporter
```

## Traces

GitHub's issue attachment endpoint rejected both ZIP and JSON content types, so the raw traces could not be attached directly. They are retained locally and can be shared through an approved artifact channel:

| Trace | Size | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Electron 42.8.0 good JSON trace | 100.67 MB | `CDD566E02D1EC87D8C7F5FEE251DB824880E1347F9415C447E073FA944A588D6` |
| Electron 42.8.1 bad JSON trace | 100.98 MB | `F101DCE0EDC32BD6C229F284B65D0A417CD2F3F46E84E75AA8F6E3F4AE61BB04` |

Compressed copies are 9.84 MB and 9.82 MB respectively.

## Mitigation

#331670 coalesces one repeated VS Code forced-layout hotspot and conservatively recovers 5-14 ms, but it does not address the underlying Electron/Blink regression.

## Expected

Electron patch updates should not make the same Windows renderer forced-layout workload approximately 32% slower or add 50+ ms to VS Code startup with an identical application.

title: Coalesce pane composite bar layout updates

labels.name: layout
labels.description: General VS Code workbench layout issues

body:
## Background

This change comes from a local investigation of Windows desktop startup performance from July 1 through August 18:

- Inventoried 154 published Insiders builds.
- Ran a 25-build randomized coarse sweep with repeated anchor sentinels.
- Confirmed the primary August boundary with interleaved A/B/A measurements.
- Localized one regression to the Electron 42.8.0 -> 42.8.1 transition.
- Reproduced the renderer regression with the identical VS Code app on official Electron runtimes.

A minimal renderer benchmark isolates the underlying runtime change:

| Electron | Forced layout | Cold JS | Warm JS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 42.8.0 | 110.0 ms | 1.2 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.8.1 | 145.2 ms | 1.2 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.9.3 | 143.5 ms | 1.1 ms | 6.5 ms |

The Blink layout regression persists in Electron 42.9.3, so this PR mitigates one forced-layout hotspot in the workbench.

Startup CPU profiles map the hottest width read to:

```text
ActionBar.getWidth
<- ToolBar.getItemsWidth
<- AbstractPaneCompositePart.getToolbarWidth
<- AbstractPaneCompositePart.layoutCompositeBar
<- AbstractPaneCompositePart.onTitleAreaUpdate
```

Each title-action update synchronously relaid out the composite bar and read every toolbar item's `clientWidth`.

## Change

Coalesce title-action-driven composite-bar layouts to one animation frame. A real synchronous part layout cancels any pending frame and computes the same final layout immediately.

This preserves the final UI state while avoiding redundant intermediate width measurements during startup.

## Performance

Fixed/unfixed traces on the same source revision and Electron runtime:

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ActionBar.getWidth` CPU self-time | 56.9 ms | 5.9 ms | **-51.0 ms** |
| Forced style/layout | 230.1 ms | 215.9 ms | **-14.2 ms** |
| Style update | 136.6 ms | 122.8 ms | **-13.7 ms** |

Non-instrumented A/fix/A source-build measurements:

- Workbench startup marker: **5-9 ms faster**
- Total dev startup: 53-60 ms faster, though most of that larger number is development module-loading variance and is not attributed to this change.
- Baseline control drift: 7 ms.

The conservative expected product win is **5-14 ms** on this Windows host under Electron 42.8.1.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\test\browser\parts\compositePart.test.ts --run src\vs\base\test\browser\ui\toolbar\toolbar.test.ts`
  - 9 passing
- Lifecycle and diff reviews found no significant issues.

title: agentHost: keep Agent Merge monitoring sessions without a client
body:
## Problem

Agent Merge only ran while a client had the session open and subscribed. Enabling it and then closing or navigating away from the session silently stopped the autonomous repair/merge work until the session was reopened, and a session enabled but never opened in the client never started monitoring at all.

## What changed

The Agent Host now keeps an Agent-Merge-enabled session resident on its own, independent of any client.

**Session hold (`AgentMergeController`)**
- The controller owns a hold on the sessions it monitors, maintained eagerly at its own state transitions and exposed as `holdsSession()`.
- `AgentService` skips idle eviction and empty-session GC for a held session, and re-arms the release when `onDidReleaseHold` reports the hold ended — so disable, archive, and terminal states (merged/closed PR, branch retargeted, attempt budget exhausted) return the session to normal eviction rather than pinning it for the life of the host.
- Tracking the hold at transitions rather than lazily on query keeps the answer correct for a session the host has never had reason to evict.

**Enablement index (orchestrator database)**
- Enablement is mirrored into an index of session URIs in the orchestrator database's existing `metadata` table, so startup finds the few monitored sessions with one query plus a single-row registry lookup each, instead of opening every per-session database. This matters at scale: 1000 sessions with 2 enabled previously meant 1000 database opens.
- Enable, disable, archive, and delete all maintain the index. Delete clears it in the same transaction that removes the session; archive clears it from the action. Stale entries (left by a crash) self-heal — an entry whose session is unregistered or archived is dropped on the next pass instead of restored.

**Startup / discovery**
- Provider registration, and turning the global feature on, restore the indexed sessions so their controllers resume. Monitoring therefore survives a host restart and works for a session never opened in this client.

Both local and remote Agent Hosts run this controller in their own process, so the behavior is provider-neutral and applies to both.

## Security

The index is a derived pointer only. It stores a URI and grants nothing: enablement and all host-owned target state (bound branch/PR, comment watermark, attempt budgets) are still read from session config, and `agentMerge.controller` remains blocked from client writes at the dispatch boundary.

## Tests

New `Agent Merge durable session monitoring` suite covering:
- stays resident after the last unsubscribe, and is released once disabled;
- enablement recorded in the host index rather than per-session databases;
- resumes on a fresh host with no client opening it, and is released once disabled;
- archived session dropped from the index instead of restored;
- index cleanup on archive and on delete;
- archived session released like any other idle session.

Each new assertion was verified to fail against the pre-fix behavior.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` on `src/tsconfig.json`: clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: clean
- ESLint on changed files: clean
- `AgentService (node dispatcher)` 325 passing, `AgentSessionRegistry` 23 passing, `AgentMerge` 6 passing

Note: `npm run hygiene` fails in this worktree on a pre-existing `check-package-json` path bug (`C:\C:\...`), reproduced identically on a clean tree, unrelated to this change.

## Reviewer notes

- No schema migration: the index lives in the existing `metadata` table. Sessions enabled *before* this change are not indexed and resume the first time they are opened, which re-indexes them. An eager one-time backfill was deliberately left out since it reintroduces the full scan this change removes.
- `unregisterSession` became a transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) so the session row and its index entry are removed atomically, matching `tombstoneAndUnregisterSession`.

title: create_file tool reports success on /memories/ virtual paths but writes nothing (silent no-op)
body:
**Type: Bug**

## Summary

The `create_file` tool silently no-ops when given a `/memories/...` filePath (the virtual filesystem exposed by the memory tool). It returns **"The following files were successfully edited"** but no file is created anywhere on disk — not at a literal `/memories/` path, and not in the physical memory store. The agent (and user) get false confirmation that memory was persisted.

## Reproduction

1. Agent-mode session where the memory tool is available (system prompt describes `/memories/` user/session/repo scopes).
2. Agent calls `create_file` with `filePath: /memories/repo/test-note.md` (any content).
3. Tool response: success — "The following files were successfully edited: /memories/repo/test-note.md".
4. Verification:
   - `ls /memories` -> `No such file or directory` (path is virtual, never created literally)
   - Physical memory store `~/.vscode-server/data/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/GitHub.copilot-chat/memory-tool/memories/repo/` does **not** contain the file
   - Full-disk `find / -name "test-note*"` returns nothing

Observed twice in one session (2026-08-19). Both attempts reported success; both wrote nothing.

## Control: memory tool works

The memory tool's own `create` command, given the same path, writes correctly — the file appears in the physical store immediately (verified with `ls` + `head` on disk). The store is healthy; only `create_file` mishandles the virtual path.

## Expected behavior

Either:

- `create_file` rejects `/memories/...` paths with an error directing the agent to the memory tool, **or**
- the write is routed into the memory store.

It must not return success without writing anything — silent data loss with a false confirmation is the worst outcome. Agents that maintain persistent memory via file tools will silently lose everything on session end.

## Impact

- Agent believes memory was saved; knowledge is gone next session.
- No error surfaces anywhere — detecting it requires explicit on-disk verification.
- Affects any agent instructed to keep notes/memory files via the standard file tools.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| VS Code | 1.133.0 (commit a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960) |
| Connection | `code tunnel` (CLI server, Linux x86_64 headless) |
| Copilot Chat (bundled) | 0.61.0 |
| OS | Linux (Debian 13, kernel 6.12) |
| Mode | Agent mode, third-party model via Copilot |

## Related

- #12924 (closed as not_planned) — `create_file` writing 0-byte files on **real** paths; this report is a distinct variant: **virtual** `/memories/` paths where nothing at all is written.
- microsoft/vscode#328189 — same family of Copilot write-tool dispatch issues.

> ### Steps to Reproduce

> 1. Install an extension or plugin that contributes a chat customization (an instruction, skill, prompt, …).
> 2. Open the **Customizations** editor and select that item.
> 3. Invoke **Open** from its context menu.

> 
> ```ts
> function extractSource(context: AICustomizationContext): AICustomizationSource | undefined {
> 	if (URI.isUri(context) || typeof context === 'string') {
> 		return undefined;
> 	}
> 	return context.storage;   // <-- the menu context has `source`, not `storage`
> }
> ```
> 
> The context object built by `aiCustomizationListWidget.ts` (both the inline action bar and the right-click menu) is:
> 
> ```ts
> const context: Record<string, unknown> = {
> 	uri: element.uri.toString(),
> 	name: element.name,
> 	promptType: element.promptType,
> 	source: element.source,          // <-- `source`
> 	pluginUri: element.pluginUri?.toString(),
> 	itemId: element.id,
> };
> ```
> 
> There is no `storage` property, so `extractSource()` always returns `undefined`. It type-checks only because `AICustomizationContext` has an `[key: string]: unknown` index signature and declares `storage?: PromptsStorage` — a field nothing ever populates.
> 
> ### Impact
> 
> `extractSource()` has two call sites:
> 
> - **Open** (`aiCustomizationManagement.openFile`) — the read-only guard `source === extension || source === plugin` never fires. This is the user-visible bug above. The **Open** menu item has no `when` clause, so it is offered for every item including extension- and plugin-provided ones.
> - **Delete** (`aiCustomizationManagement.delete`) — the in-action `source` guards (the plugin *"uninstall the entire plugin?"* prompt, and the *"Cannot Delete Extension File"* dialog) are dead code. **No data-loss risk**, because the Delete menu item itself is correctly gated by `WHEN_ITEM_IS_DELETABLE`, which uses the `AI_CUSTOMIZATION_ITEM_STORAGE_KEY` context key — and *that* key is correctly populated from `element.source`. The guards are unreachable defence-in-depth rather than the active protection.
> - Delete telemetry (`chatCustomizationEditor.deleteItem`) records `storage: source ?? ''`, so that dimension is always the empty string.
> 
> ### Suggested fix
> 
> Read `context.source` instead of `context.storage`, and drop the unused `storage?: PromptsStorage` field from `AICustomizationContext` so the type reflects what the widget actually sends. Note the declared return type is `AICustomizationSource` while the (unused) field is typed `PromptsStorage` — worth reconciling at the same time.
>

title: Chat input pills: reusable widget, artifacts, customizations and visibility
body:
Reworks the pill row above the Agents-window chat input, and consolidates how pills are rendered.

## What changed

**Reusable widget.** The pill row is left-aligned and horizontally scrollable, driven by a reusable observable `ChatPillsWidget` in `vs/workbench/browser`. Sessions owns every adapter from session state and menus, so the workbench layer never imports sessions.

**Metadata placement setting.** `chat.agentSessions.showSessionMetadataInInput` (default off) moves the session header metadata pills down into the input row, hides the header's second row, moves Chats into the title toolbar after New Chat, and shows read-only workspace metadata next to the session title.

**Artifacts.** New agent-host tools `add_artifact` / `remove_artifact` / `list_artifacts`, gated by `chat.artifactTools.enabled`, persisted across host restarts and streamed to the client over the session `_meta` bag. GitHub pull request and issue artifacts are promoted into the session's GitHub links instead of appearing twice; only session-created pull requests are eligible to become the main pull request.

**Customizations.** The customizations a chat used or read are derived from its output stream and surfaced in a pill; clicking an entry reveals it in the customizations editor. Detection reuses the existing chat-state subscription, caches completed turns by id, and only re-parses the in-progress turn while streaming.

**Visibility menu.** Right-clicking the row offers `Hide <pill>` for the clicked pill, then the kinds with data, then those without. Customizations and Subagents start hidden; Changes can never be hidden.

**One set of pill implementations.** Everything now renders through one base plus four implementations: icon + label, dropdown (extends icon + label), resource label, and the animated changes pill. This removes the duplicated `SessionActivityPill`, the hosted-pill wrapper and their CSS.

## Notable fixes found along the way

- `VisibleSession` forwards `ISession` properties by hand and silently dropped `artifacts`; added a generic regression test that diffs wrapper against wrapped.
- The toolbar swallowed `contextmenu` per item, so right-clicking a pill never reached the row's visibility menu — only the empty strip beside it worked.
- `focus()` did not restore the tab stop that `blur()` removed, so arrowing between pills left the row with no tabbable item and Shift+Tab could not return to it. The same bug existed in `automationsView.ts`.
- Promotion now requires a link the pull request / issue pills can actually render, so an enterprise host does not vanish from both the artifacts pill and the GitHub pills.

## Validation

`tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, stylelint and `valid-layers-check` all clean. Unit tests cover the artifact model and tools, the customization parser (ordering, de-duplication, incremental re-parse), the visibility menu and defaults, pill focus and context-menu behaviour, and the GitHub promotion rules; the local agent-host provider suite passes in full. UI verified in the component explorer.

title: chat: preserve unresolved custom mode ids
body:
This fixes a restore race for custom chat modes that are referenced by persisted input state before custom modes have finished loading.

When `setChatMode` cannot immediately resolve a persisted custom mode, it still needs to show a usable Agent/Ask fallback. Previously, later `_syncInputStateToModel()` calls persisted that fallback ID back into the model, replacing the original custom mode ID with `agent`. When `modes.onDidChange` fired, the existing `_restorePersistedCustomModeIfAvailable()` recovery path then saw a builtin mode and skipped recovery.

The fix keeps the unresolved requested mode ID separate from the displayed fallback:

- Adds `resolveChatModeOrFallback(modes, id)` to return both the displayable `mode` and an optional `unresolvedId`.
- Tracks `_unresolvedModeId` in `ChatInputPart` while the fallback is active.
- Persists `_unresolvedModeId ?? mode.id`, preserving the user's intended custom mode across syncs.
- Clears the unresolved ID on session switch.
- Avoids repeatedly resolving an ID that is already known to be unresolved in `_syncFromModel`.
- Guards `validateCurrentChatMode()` so `chat.agent.enabled: false` does not overwrite the pending custom mode ID with `ask` while the fallback is only standing in for an unresolved custom mode.

This shape preserves intent instead of adding another retry loop: the model continues to hold the user's requested mode ID, while the UI can temporarily render a safe fallback until the normal `modes.onDidChange` recovery path has the information it needs. Unresolved `mode.id` is already an expected condition for agent-host/custom modes that register later and for missing customizations, and consumers validate before use.

Testing:
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npx eslint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatModes.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatModeService.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatModeService.test.ts`
- Chat common test sweep: 83 passing
- Full compile: 0 errors
- Manual GUI check: custom agents surface correctly and the selected custom agent survives restart

Added coverage for:
- Resolving a known custom mode
- Falling back to Agent while returning the unresolved custom mode ID
- Recovering after the custom mode becomes available
- Falling back to Ask when Agent is unavailable

Note: an attempted without-fix baseline using an empty session did not reproduce because empty sessions already have a separate recovery path. This PR targets restored sessions with persisted input state/history.

title: fix: guard stale cursor line in toInlineSuggestion (fixes #331652)
body:
### Summary
`toInlineSuggestion` throws `Error: Illegal value for line` when computing whether an async next-edit-suggestion (NES) can be rendered as ghost text. The crash is `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` in `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` (`isInlineSuggestion.ts:49`): `cursorPos` is the request cursor VS Code core captured when it invoked the inline-completion provider, but NES results are processed asynchronously. If the document is edited (shrinks) before the result is processed, `cursorPos.line` exceeds the current `document.lineCount`, so `lineAt` rejects it. First seen in `GitHub.copilot-chat` 0.61.0 (new anomaly, not present in 0.59.0).

Fixes microsoft/vscode#331652
Recommended reviewer: `@ulugbekna`

### Culprit Commit
`a53a3fd5160` — "Fix inline suggestion false negatives via canonical cursor-edit rebasing (#325278)" by `@ulugbekna`. This commit added `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`, which unconditionally calls `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)`. The prior implementation only touched the cursor line when the edit range already sat on it, so a stale cursor line never reached `lineAt`. This matches the "new in 0.61.0" telemetry signal.

### Code Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[VS Code core captures request cursor position] --> B[provideInlineCompletionItems]
  B --> C[async NES computation]
  C --> D[document edited/shrinks in background]
  D --> E[_provideInlineCompletionItems processes result]
  E --> F[toInlineSuggestion cursorPos document range newText]
  F --> G[advanced path calls tryRebaseAsCursorEdit]
  G --> H[doc.lineAt cursorPos.line]
  H --> I[throws Illegal value for line: cursorPos.line >= document.lineCount]
```

### Affected Files
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/isInlineSuggestion.ts` — crash site (`tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`) and entry point (`toInlineSuggestion`).
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/inlineCompletionProvider.ts:451` — sole caller; passes the async request `position` into `toInlineSuggestion`.

### Repro Steps
1. Trigger a next-edit suggestion near the end of a document with inline-completions/advanced rebasing enabled.
2. Before the async NES result is served, delete text so the document has fewer lines than the original request cursor line.
3. When the result is processed, `toInlineSuggestion` calls `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` with an out-of-range line and throws the illegal-line error.

### How the Fix Works
**Chosen approach** (`isInlineSuggestion.ts`): add a guard at the top of `toInlineSuggestion` that returns `undefined` when `cursorPos.line` is outside the valid range `[0, doc.lineCount)`. `cursorPos` crosses the VS Code core to extension boundary asynchronously (the producer of the position is core, not reachable from the extension), and by result-processing time the document may have mutated. A stale cursor means the edit was computed against a document state that no longer exists, so it genuinely cannot be rendered as ghost text — returning `undefined` is exactly the function's existing "not renderable" contract, not error suppression. The guard is placed at the single entry point that establishes the "valid cursor line in doc" precondition all helpers (`tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`, `tryAdjustNextLineInsertion`, `validateSameLineGhostText`) rely on, rather than at the individual `lineAt` crash site. No try/catch is introduced and no logging is removed. After this change, `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` at `isInlineSuggestion.ts:49` cannot receive an out-of-range `cursorPos.line` because `toInlineSuggestion` rejects it before dispatching to any helper.

**Alternatives considered**: guarding directly inside `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` around the `lineAt` call — rejected because the same stale-cursor precondition is shared by the other helpers, so the guard belongs at the common entry point; wrapping the call in try/catch — rejected because it would hide the staleness instead of expressing the not-renderable contract.

### Recommended Owner
`@ulugbekna` — author of the culprit commit `a53a3fd5160` (#325278) that introduced the unconditional `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` call in the inline-suggestion rebasing path.

- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/inlineCompletionProvider.ts:451` — sole caller; passes the async request `position` into `toInlineSuggestion`.

### Repro Steps
1. Trigger a next-edit suggestion near the end of a document with inline-completions/advanced rebasing enabled.
2. Before the async NES result is served, delete text so the document has fewer lines than the original request cursor line.
3. When the result is processed, `toInlineSuggestion` calls `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` with an out-of-range line and throws the illegal-line error.

### How the Fix Works
**Chosen approach** (`isInlineSuggestion.ts`): add a guard at the top of `toInlineSuggestion` that returns `undefined` when `cursorPos.line` is outside the valid range `[0, doc.lineCount)`. `cursorPos` crosses the VS Code core to extension boundary asynchronously (the producer of the position is core, not reachable from the extension), and by result-processing time the document may have mutated. A stale cursor means the edit was computed against a document state that no longer exists, so it genuinely cannot be rendered as ghost text — returning `undefined` is exactly the function's existing "not renderable" contract, not error suppression. The guard is placed at the single entry point that establishes the "valid cursor line in doc" precondition all helpers (`tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`, `tryAdjustNextLineInsertion`, `validateSameLineGhostText`) rely on, rather than at the individual `lineAt` crash site. No try/catch is introduced and no logging is removed. After this change, `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` at `isInlineSuggestion.ts:49` cannot receive an out-of-range `cursorPos.line` because `toInlineSuggestion` rejects it before dispatching to any helper.

**Alternatives considered**: guarding directly inside `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` around the `lineAt` call — rejected because the same stale-cursor precondition is shared by the other helpers, so the guard belongs at the common entry point; wrapping the call in try/catch — rejected because it would hide the staleness instead of expressing the not-renderable contract.

### Recommended Owner
`@ulugbekna` — author of the culprit commit `a53a3fd5160` (#325278) that introduced the unconditional `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` call in the inline-suggestion rebasing path.

title: Agent Host session restore races initial provider catalog migration after update

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified

labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in
- VS Code Version: Latest Insiders after update (2026-08-18)
- OS Version: macOS
- Feature: Agents Window / restored Agent Host Copilot session
- Selected model: GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Agent Host debug bundle captured locally; relevant sanitized timeline below

## Summary

After updating VS Code Insiders, the Agents Window can restore its previously active session into a persistent error state:

> Couldn't open session
>
> Session not found on backend: `copilotcli:/7b1237b7-8b12-40d6-ba88-e9ce08675ac5`

The session is valid and loads successfully after navigating to another session and back.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have an existing Agent Host Copilot session selected in the Agents Window.
2. Update/restart VS Code Insiders so the window and Agent Host restore their previous state.
3. Observe that the restored active session displays `Session not found on backend`.
4. Navigate to another session and then back to the original session.
5. The original session now loads normally.

## Expected

The restored active session waits for Agent Host startup/catalog initialization and loads without user navigation.

## Actual

The initial session subscription receives a transient `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` error. The chat model renders and retains that load failure until reopening the session triggers a fresh subscription.

## Correlated log timeline

All timestamps below are local time on 2026-08-18:

- `18:23:42.971`: Agent Host starts the initial `listSessions` computation.
- `18:24:11.096`: Copilot finishes enumerating 2,421 legacy sessions.
- `18:24:11.101`: Three subscriptions for the restored session fail with `Session not found on backend`.
- `18:24:11.102`: The window logs `Failed to subscribe to existing session` and creates the chat model containing the visible load error.
- `18:24:12.079`: Copilot successfully resumes the backing chat for the same session.
- `18:24:12.173`: Agent Host restores the same session with 10 turns.
- `18:24:12.511`: Agent Host reports the session restored successfully.

This confirms the session is not missing. The subscription arrived about one second before initial provider catalog migration/registration completed.

## Root cause

`AgentService.listSessions()` waits for provider registration-time legacy migration through `_awaitInitialProviderMigration()`, but `AgentService.restoreSession()` did not. A restored editor can therefore call `restoreSession()` while the provider's initial native-session catalog migration is still in flight. Provider metadata lookup returns no result during that window, causing a false `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` response that becomes sticky in the UI.

## Proposed fix

At the Agent Host boundary, wait for the initial migration of the session's provider before reading its registry entry and provider metadata in `restoreSession()`.

A local fix:

- extracted provider-specific waiting/retry logic into `_awaitInitialProviderMigrationForProvider(provider)`;
- reused it from `listSessions()`;
- awaited it in `_doRestoreSession()` after the tombstone check and before registry/metadata lookup;
- added a regression test where `listChatsToMigrate()` is intentionally blocked while `restoreSession()` begins, then verifies restore succeeds once migration completes.

Keeping the fix host-side avoids a UI retry timer and covers all Agent Host clients.

## Validation

The following focused tests pass locally:

- `waits for initial provider migration before restoring a session` (new regression test)
- `rejects restoring a session that has been explicitly deleted (tombstoned) without resurrecting it`
- `listSessions rejects an unavailable migration catalog and retries it on the next call`

A search found #331006, but that issue describes editor Chat actively destroying a valid standalone Agent session and creating phantom IDs. This report is a separate startup ordering race: the same session restores successfully moments later and no destruction occurs.

title: Preserve user-defined casing for File Explorer workspace titles
body:
This pull request improves how the File Explorer displays workspace names by ensuring that user-provided workspace names are shown with their original casing, rather than being automatically capitalized or uppercased. It introduces new logic and CSS classes to distinguish between user-named workspaces and system-generated or untitled workspaces, updates the Explorer view logic, and adds comprehensive tests to verify the new behavior.

Key changes include:

### Explorer View Logic and API

* Added the `shouldPreserveWorkspaceNameCase` function to determine if the original casing of a workspace name should be preserved, based on workspace type and configuration. This function is used to apply appropriate styling only to user-named workspaces. (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerView.ts`)
* Introduced new CSS class constants `PRESERVE_WORKSPACE_NAME_CASE_CLASS` and `PRESERVE_MERGED_WORKSPACE_NAME_CASE_CLASS` for marking DOM elements that should preserve name casing. (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerView.ts`)
* Updated the `ExplorerView` class to manage and update these classes on the relevant DOM nodes when the workspace changes, the view is shown/hidden, or the header visibility changes. (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerView.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7aedf2ce39d5f3c6edca567c1e25b828a9b8fc0eaa9d47b12be7093eb9747c23R211) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7aedf2ce39d5f3c6edca567c1e25b828a9b8fc0eaa9d47b12be7093eb9747c23L214-R242) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7aedf2ce39d5f3c6edca567c1e25b828a9b8fc0eaa9d47b12be7093eb9747c23L234-R263) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7aedf2ce39d5f3c6edca567c1e25b828a9b8fc0eaa9d47b12be7093eb9747c23R286-R303) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7aedf2ce39d5f3c6edca567c1e25b828a9b8fc0eaa9d47b12be7093eb9747c23L288-R359)

### Styling

* Updated the Modern UI CSS so that only DOM elements with the new classes (`preserve-workspace-name-case` or `preserve-merged-workspace-name-case`) will display workspace names with their original casing. Untitled and system-generated names continue to use standard capitalization. (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/browser/media/fontRamp.css`)

### Testing

* Added a unit test for `shouldPreserveWorkspaceNameCase` to ensure it correctly identifies when to preserve the workspace name's casing, covering empty, folder, untitled, and named workspace scenarios. (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/test/browser/explorerView.test.ts`)
* Updated Modern UI contribution tests to account for the new CSS classes and verify that the correct `text-transform` styles are applied to the Explorer titles and pane headers in various scenarios. (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d998c5a9020cea4f29150549e3a6bde9b6746696afc7dba7a0a8ed03185efb18R23-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d998c5a9020cea4f29150549e3a6bde9b6746696afc7dba7a0a8ed03185efb18L285-R304) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d998c5a9020cea4f29150549e3a6bde9b6746696afc7dba7a0a8ed03185efb18R318-R320) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d998c5a9020cea4f29150549e3a6bde9b6746696afc7dba7a0a8ed03185efb18R339-R341)

These changes ensure that the File Explorer more accurately reflects user intent regarding workspace naming, improving both consistency and user experience.

title: Fix keyword color too similar to function color in 2026 themes
body:
## Problem

Fixes #331622.

In the **2026 Dark Theme**, keywords (`if`, `import`, `try`, `except`, `for`, `while`, etc.) are visually hard to distinguish from function names, as reported with a screenshot in the issue.

## Root cause

`2026-dark.json` defines its own `tokenColors` rule for the generic `"keyword"` scope (`#ff7b72`, coral-red). However, `dark_plus.json` (an ancestor via the theme `include` chain: `2026-dark.json` → `dark_modern.json` → `dark_plus.json`) already defines a **more specific** rule for `"keyword.control"` (`#C586C0`, magenta).

VS Code's TextMate scope matching always prefers the most specific matching selector, regardless of which theme in the include chain defined it. Since most real keywords use scopes like `keyword.control.flow.python` or `keyword.control.import.python`, they match `keyword.control` (2 segments) rather than the theme's own `keyword` (1 segment) rule — so the inherited `#C586C0` wins over the theme's intended `#ff7b72`.

`#C586C0` (magenta) sits visually very close to the theme's `entity.name.function` color (`#D2A8FF`, lavender) — both are pastel purple/magenta tones on the same near-black background, which is exactly the collision reported in the issue.

I confirmed this by downloading the screenshot attached to the issue and sampling its pixels directly: `import`/`from`/`as` render as `#C586C0`, while the called/imported function name renders as `#D2A8FF`.

The same issue exists in `2026-light.json` (`keyword` = `#cf222e`, shadowed by `light_plus.json`'s `keyword.control` = `#AF00DB`, close to that theme's `entity.name.function` = `#8250df`), so I fixed both for consistency.

## Fix

Minimal, one rule changed per theme: add `"keyword.control"` alongside `"keyword"` in each theme's own `tokenColors`, so the theme's intended color wins for control-flow keywords too — the same pattern the theme already uses elsewhere (e.g. its `storage.modifier.*` overrides).

```diff
 {
-    "scope": "keyword",
+    "scope": [
+        "keyword",
+        "keyword.control"
+    ],
     "settings": {
         "foreground": "#ff7b72"
     }
 },
```

(analogous change in `2026-light.json` with `#cf222e`)

## Validation

There are no existing automated tests asserting specific theme color values in this repo, so none were added — theme color changes are conventionally validated visually. To verify without a full Electron build, I wrote a small script that replicates the actual theme `include`-merge and TextMate scope-specificity resolution logic from `colorThemeData.ts`, and confirmed:

| Scope | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `keyword.control.flow.python` | `#C586C0` | `#ff7b72` |
| `keyword.control.import.python` | `#C586C0` | `#ff7b72` |
| `entity.name.function` | `#D2A8FF` (unchanged) | `#D2A8FF` (unchanged) |

I also rendered a before/after swatch confirming the visual improvement, and re-verified the equivalent scopes/colors for the light theme fix.

## Test plan

- [x] Confirmed root cause via pixel-sampling the issue's screenshot
- [x] Confirmed fix via scope-resolution simulation matching production merge logic
- [x] `git diff` reviewed — only the two theme JSON files touched, one rule each

title: Copilot in WSL asks permission to read files inside the current workspace
body:
# Copilot in WSL asks permission to read files inside the current workspace

## Environment

* Windows 11
* WSL2
* Ubuntu
* VS Code: 1.134.0
* GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.62.0
* Workspace opened using Remote - WSL
* Workspace path:

```text
/home/yzh/projects/INCtime
```

## Problem

GitHub Copilot correctly identifies the current workspace as:

```text
/home/yzh/projects/INCtime
```

However, when the agent uses the Read tool on the same path, VS Code shows:

```text
Allow reading file outside of workspace?
```

For example, the tool input is:

```json
{
  "pattern": "**/*",
  "paths": "/home/yzh/projects/INCtime"
}
```

or:

```json
{
  "path": "/home/yzh/projects/INCtime"
}
```

The requested path is exactly the current VS Code workspace, so it should not be classified as an external folder.

## What I verified

The workspace is opened correctly using WSL:

```text
Remote: WSL: Ubuntu
```

`pwd` returns:

```text
/home/yzh/projects/INCtime
```

VS Code Workspace Trust also lists:

```text
WSL: Ubuntu
/home/yzh/projects/INCtime
```

GitHub Copilot Chat is running on:

```text
WSL: Ubuntu
```

Copilot itself also reports:

```text
My workspace is /home/yzh/projects/INCtime
```

Despite all of this, the Read tool still asks for permission to access a file "outside of workspace".

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Ubuntu WSL.
2. Run:

```bash
cd /home/yzh/projects/INCtime
code .
```

3. Confirm the VS Code window shows:

```text
WSL: Ubuntu
```

4. Open GitHub Copilot Chat in Agent mode.
5. Start a new chat.
6. Ask:

```text
Read all files in this project
```

7. Copilot attempts to read:

```text
/home/yzh/projects/INCtime
```

8. VS Code displays:

```text
Allow reading file outside of workspace?
```

## Expected behavior

Files under:

```text
/home/yzh/projects/INCtime
```

should be recognized as files inside the current workspace and should not require "outside workspace" permission.

## Actual behavior

The permission checker treats the current WSL workspace root as an external folder.

## Additional notes

I have already tested:

* Workspace Trust enabled
* Opening VS Code from WSL using `code .`
* Starting a new Copilot chat session
* Reloading the VS Code window
* Confirming Copilot Chat runs in `WSL: Ubuntu`
* `chat.additionalReadAccessFolders`
* Default / Bypass Approvals settings

The workspace path and requested Read path are identical.

title: Cap External Agent Sessions to 30 Days (replace `all`, enforce ingest/prune retention)
body:
## Description

This changes external-session visibility from unbounded to a strict 30-day retention model to reduce slow session surfacing/filtering and keep catalog size bounded. The `all` mode is removed from user-facing options and behavior, while legacy persisted `all` values are migrated/treated as `last30Days`.

- **Mode and settings surface**
	- Replaced `ChatExternalSessionsMode.All` with `ChatExternalSessionsMode.Last30Days`.
	- Updated external session picker/menu labels and ordering to use **Last 30 Days** as the terminal option.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No — this is not reproducible with extensions disabled because GitHub Copilot Chat (the extension providing the MCP webview host) is itself required to reproduce it. The bug is in VS Code's own MCP app webview CSP construction, which only runs when Copilot Chat's MCP Apps feature is active.

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (darwin arm64)
- OS Version: macOS (darwin arm64)

### Steps to Reproduce:

1. Connect an MCP server whose UI resource renders a map using MapLibre GL JS (e.g. CARTO's MCP server, over HTTP, with Copilot Chat 0.61.0 as the MCP Apps host).
2. Ask the agent to show data on a map (a tool call that returns an MCP UI resource with a MapLibre-based map widget).
3. Observe: the data layer renders, but the basemap never paints — the map area stays blank behind the data. No error is surfaced in the chat UI.
4. Open the webview's DevTools console (Help > Toggle Developer Tools) and see:
```
Creating a worker from 'blob:vscode-webview://…' violates the following Content
Security Policy directive: "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <domains>".
Note that 'worker-src' was not explicitly set, so 'script-src' is used as a
fallback. The action has been blocked.
```

### Root cause
The MCP app webview's injected Content-Security-Policy has no `worker-src` directive. Per spec, when `worker-src` is unset the browser falls back to `script-src`, which has no `blob:` scheme - so any MCP app that spawns a Web Worker from a `blob:` URL (e.g. MapLibre GL JS's tile-parsing workers) is blocked.

Confirmed directly in source: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatMcpAppModel.ts`, in `_injectPreamble`. The full directive list built there is `default-src`, `script-src`, `style-src`, `connect-src`, `img-src`, `font-src`, `media-src`, `frame-src`, `object-src`, `base-uri` - `worker-src` is absent.

### Suggested fix
Add `worker-src 'self' blob:;` to the CSP content string, alongside the existing directives.

### Related
- This is not fixable from the MCP resource side, and does not require an MCP Apps spec change - the reference host implementation (`examples/basic-host/serve.ts` in `modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`) already sets `worker-src 'self' blob:` unconditionally.
- Separately, `modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps#566` proposes a `workerDomains` field for resource-level control - that's an independent, optional enhancement, not a prerequisite for this fix.

title: Extension host restarts on every chat turn after an in-place update, silently resetting Copilot Chat session state (model, agent, MCP servers)
body:
## Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?

Not verified — the issue is in Copilot Chat session state, so disabling all extensions removes the observable surface. I can retest with a minimal extension set on request.

## Version

- VS Code (running processes): **1.126.0**
- VS Code (staged on disk during the session): **1.134.0**
- GitHub Copilot Chat: **0.54.0**
- OS: **Windows 11 x64**, user-scope (non-admin) install

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run VS Code for an extended period (my processes had been up for ~9 days).
2. Let the auto-updater download and stage a newer build in the background. In my case it wrote a new versioned build directory and ran the installer with `/nocloseapplications`, i.e. it did **not** require the running instance to exit.
3. Without restarting, continue using a Copilot Chat agent session that has non-default settings — a specific model, a specific reasoning effort, a custom agent, and MCP servers enabled.
4. Send several messages over the course of ~20 minutes.

## Actual Behavior

The chat session is torn down and re-created on **every turn**. Consequences, all user-visible but none surfaced as an error:

1. **Session settings silently revert to defaults each turn.** I selected a specific model at *high* reasoning effort and got *medium*. My selected custom agent was not applied — it was offered only as a delegatable subagent.
2. **MCP servers turn themselves off.** Re-enabling them between turns did not stick. `stdio`-based servers are child processes of the extension host, so each restart kills them; no MCP server processes were alive when I checked.
3. **MCP tools disappear mid-turn.** In one turn a tool call against an MCP server succeeded; a few minutes later, within the same conversation, the same tool no longer existed in the tool list. The failure mode was `No MCP client found for tool ID: <tool>`, then on retry `Tool '<tool>' does not exist`.
4. **Previously rendered output is lost** when switching between chat sessions and back, because the session is re-created rather than restored.
5. **Nothing tells the user any of this is happening.** No notification, no "reload required" prompt, no error. The model appears to ignore instructions and behave erratically, so the natural conclusion is that the *model* or the *user's configuration* is broken. I spent a full troubleshooting cycle chasing a non-existent MCP configuration problem before finding the real cause.

## Expected Behavior

- If an update is staged that leaves the running extension host inconsistent, **prompt the user to restart** (as VS Code already does for extension updates) instead of degrading silently.
- Chat session settings — model, reasoning effort, selected agent, MCP enablement — should either **survive** an extension host restart, or the user should be **told** they were reset.
- If MCP servers die because their host restarted, surface that as a **visible, actionable error** rather than silently removing tools from the model's tool list mid-conversation.

## Diagnostic Evidence

The Copilot Chat debug log for the affected session contains **five `session_start` events and nothing else** — no model requests, no tool calls, no customization-loading events. The timestamps match my five messages to within ~2 seconds each:

| session_start | user message |
|---|---|
| 13:57:47 | 13:57:49 |
| 14:00:49 | 14:00:49 |
| 14:05:57 | 14:05:59 |
| 14:10:15 | 14:10:17 |
| 14:19:53 | 14:19:55 |

I checked four separate sessions in this workspace: **all** contain only `session_start` events. So conversation-level diagnostic logging captured nothing at all, which made this substantially harder to diagnose than it should have been. That looks like a second, independent bug — the logging paths appear not to match the swapped-out build.

Supporting observations at the OS level:

- 11 VS Code processes running, all started 9 days before the session, reporting **1.126.0**.
- A build directory for **1.134.0** created *during* the session (~2h before the failures started).
- The installer process still alive ~2h20m later, launched with `/nocloseapplications`.
- **Seven** versioned build directories accumulated in the install folder. Notably, the running extension host was loading some of its bundled assets from a build directory dated **~2 months earlier** than the newest one — so more than one version mismatch was in play simultaneously.
- No MCP server processes alive, despite MCP being configured and having worked earlier in the session.

## Additional Context

A full restart of VS Code is the obvious workaround, but the user has no way to know that's what's needed. Every symptom points at the AI or at the user's own configuration:

- the model "downgrading" itself,
- a custom agent being "ignored",
- MCP toggles that "won't stay on",
- tools that exist in one message and not the next.

The underlying cause — a background update that left the running instance inconsistent — is completely invisible from the chat UI. Even a generic "VS Code was updated in the background; reload to restore full functionality" notification would have prevented the entire investigation.

title: Fix extension command titles losing localization after install/update
body:
## Description

Fixes #330908 — Extension command titles lose localization after installing/updating an extension until full restart.

### Root Cause

When an extension is installed or updated while VS Code is running, the **incremental scan** path (`scanExistingExtension` → `createExtensionScannerInput`) is invoked **without a `language` argument** (see `scanLocalExtension` in `extensionManagementService.ts`, which calls `scanExistingExtension(location, type, { includeInvalid: true })`).

In `createExtensionScannerInput`, the `language` was only used for `translations` via `language ?? platform.language`, but the value stored in `ExtensionScannerInput.language` was the **raw `undefined`**. As a result, `findMessageBundles` hit this early return:

```ts
if (nlsConfiguration.devMode || nlsConfiguration.pseudo || !nlsConfiguration.language) {
    return c({ localized: joinPath(extensionLocation, 'package.nls.json'), original: null });
}
```

…so `package.nls.<locale>.json` was never loaded for the updated extension, and the manifest `%key%` references were not translated. Command titles reverted to English until a full restart (which triggers a full scan with the correct language).

The remote path (`remoteExtensionsScanner.ts`) already passes `{ language }` correctly — only the local incremental path was affected.

### Fix

Fall back to `platform.language` when no explicit language is passed, so the language stored in `ExtensionScannerInput` matches what was already used for `translations`:

```ts
language = language ?? platform.language;
const translations = await this.getTranslations(language);
```

### Validation

- Added test: `scan existing extension without language uses platform language for nls` — verifies that scanning without a language still localizes the manifest using the platform language.
- 30 tests passing in `extensionsScannerService.test.ts` (the single pre-existing failure `scan system extensions include additional builtin extensions` is an environment-only issue with bare mocha — `Cannot determine URI for module id!` — unrelated to this change; it fails identically on `main`).
