title: fix: guard identity lookup for root element in getDataNode (fixes #330873)
body:
Fixes #330873

### Summary

In `AsyncDataTree.getDataNode(element: TInput | T)`, when a node lookup fails (`!node`), the error-enrichment path unconditionally casts `element` to `T` and invokes `this.identityProvider.getId(element as T)`.

When `element` is the root input (for example in `ExplorerView` where `TInput = ExplorerItem[]` and `T = ExplorerItem`), `element` is an array that lacks `.getId()`. This throws `TypeError: s.getId is not a function`, which masks the intended `TreeError` and triggers unhandled runtime error telemetry crashes.

### Changes
1. **`src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts`**:
   - Only evaluate `this.identityProvider.getId(element as T)` when `element !== this.root.element`.
2. **`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerView.ts`**:
   - Defensively verify `typeof stat?.getId === 'function'` in `identityProvider.getId` to safely handle arrays and fallback objects without throwing.
3. **`src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.test.ts`**:
   - Added unit test asserting that calling `updateChildren` with an unknown root input element properly throws `TreeError` instead of a `TypeError` when an `identityProvider` is configured.

title: sessions: fix: guard chat grid neighbor lookup before layout
body:
Fixes #331616

## What changed

This change tracks whether the current Agents window session grid has completed its first layout. Reconciliation uses logical group order until geometric neighbor queries are safe.

It also adds a regression test for opening and focusing a session whose active chat is a child chat with a `parentChat`.

## User-visible failure

Opening an affected session could leave the chat area partially initialized:

- The main chat tab was visible.
- No tab was active.
- The active child chat tab was missing.
- The **Start a parallel conversation** composer was rendered and focused.

Clicking the visible main tab repaired the view and caused the remaining chat tab to appear.

## Root cause

`ChatGroupsView.setSession` previously created and attached a new `SerializableGrid`, installed an `autorun` that synchronously invoked `_reconcile`, and only then called `_applyLayout`.

When the outer `ChatGroupsView` had already been laid out and the session's active chat had a `parentChat`, reconciliation attempted to place the child beside its parent. `_findAdjacentGroup` called `SerializableGrid.getNeighborViews`, but the new grid had not received its first `layout()` call and threw:

```text
Can't call getNeighborViews before first layout
```

The main chat had already been assigned before the exception. Since those observable writes were not rolled back, the UI retained the main tab while failing to assign or activate the child chat, producing the partial state above.

## Why this fix

The current grid resets a `_gridDidLayout` flag when the session changes and sets it after `layout()` completes. `_findAdjacentGroup` only calls `getNeighborViews` once that flag is true; before then it uses its existing logical group-order fallback.

This retains the original reconcile-before-layout ordering, so the resolved chat view is laid out once and the transient parallel-conversation composer is not laid out before being replaced.

The change does not add exception handling or a focus-specific workaround.

## Validation

- Added a regression covering an already-laid-out view with an active child chat, including the replacement chat view's layout and document-scoped focus.
- The regression records layout calls: one for the resolved chat and zero for the transient composer.
- All 13 `ChatGroupsView` unit tests pass.
- Targeted ESLint passes.
- Client TypeScript type-check passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Manual end-to-end verification on macOS against the fixed source build:
  - Created a session with a main chat and active parallel child chat, switched away, and reopened it.
  - Both tabs were present, the child was active and rendered, focus was inside its chat input, and the parallel-conversation composer was absent.
  - The renderer log contained no `Can't call getNeighborViews before first layout` error.

title: Agents window opens the parallel conversation composer instead of the active child chat

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
## Description

In the Agents window, opening an existing session can show and focus the **Start a parallel conversation** composer instead of the session's active chat.

The UI is left partially initialized: the main chat tab is visible, but no tab is active and other chats are missing. Clicking the visible main tab repairs the view and causes the remaining chat tab to appear.

This affects sessions whose active chat is a child chat with a `parentChat`, after the chat-groups surface has already received its initial outer layout.

Observed in VS Code Insiders commit `d1d996042bdf0cfccbe36f37c2052c314ed159d5` on macOS.

## Reproduction steps

Prerequisite: have an agent session containing a main chat and a child chat whose `origin.parentChat` references the main chat, with the child chat active.

1. Open the Agents window.
2. Open or display another session so that the chat-groups surface completes its initial layout.
3. In the session list, select the session whose active chat is the child chat.
4. Observe the chat area and keyboard focus.

## Expected behavior

The session opens with its active child chat selected, rendered, and focused. Both the main and child chat tabs are present.

## Actual behavior

The main chat tab is visible, but no tab is active. The child chat tab is missing, and focus lands in the **Start a parallel conversation** composer.

Clicking the visible main chat tab causes the real chat contents and the missing chat tab to appear.

The renderer logs this error at the time of the session click:

```text
Can't call getNeighborViews before first layout
    at SerializableGrid.getNeighborViews
    at ChatGroupsView._findAdjacentGroup
    at ChatGroupsView._reconcile
    at ChatGroupsView.setSession
```

## Root cause

**Confirmed root cause:** `ChatGroupsView.setSession` creates and attaches a new `SerializableGrid`, then installs a synchronous reconciliation autorun before applying the existing outer layout to that new grid.

When the active chat has a `parentChat`, reconciliation attempts to place it adjacent to its parent. Because the outer `ChatGroupsView` has already been laid out, `_findAdjacentGroup` calls `SerializableGrid.getNeighborViews`. The newly created grid has not received its first `layout()` call yet, so that method throws.

Reconciliation has already assigned the main chat before the exception. Those observable writes are not rolled back, leaving exactly the observed partial UI: the main tab is present, the active child is unassigned, and the group renders and focuses its parallel-conversation composer.

The grid-layout implementation was introduced in #330848.

## Additional context

The error occurred repeatedly in the affected Insiders renderer log. The workaround is to click the visible main chat tab, which changes the active chat and allows reconciliation to complete.

The fix tracks whether the current grid has completed its first layout and uses logical group order instead of geometric neighbor queries until then. This preserves the original reconciliation-before-layout ordering. A regression test reproduces the exact active-child and already-laid-out state.

Fixes #331013

Modern UI editor tabs sit in a uniform 4px gutter (24px pill in a 32px title). Bottom-panel title tabs did not: classic UI still draws a 1px top border on `.part.panel.bottom .composite.title` (`panelpart.css`). title: agentHost: migrate legacy Copilot CLI sessions on open, not just in the list
body:
Fixes #331266

## The problem

A legacy Copilot CLI session has two addresses: `copilotcli:/<id>` (extension host) and `agent-host-copilotcli:/<id>` (agent host). Only opening the second one migrates it. Opening the first works — you get your session — but it silently never migrates,
so you are in the same position next time.

The first attempt at this filtered the **session list**: wait for agent host discovery, then show only the agent-host row. That covers clicking a row, and nothing else.

Sessions are addressed by **URI** everywhere else, because a URI is what's durable:

| Path | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatEditorInput.resolve` | Reopening a window with a chat editor open |
| `_restoreVisibleSessions` | Agents window restoring its grid |
| `openSessionByResource` | Session links, hover, picker, Open as Editor |
| `openSession` | Commands and direct navigation |

None of these consult the list. Window restore is the common case and needs no unusual action, which is why it was easy to miss.

## The approach

Redirect the legacy address rather than trying to hide every reference to it.

When anything opens `copilotcli:/<id>`, we derive the agent-host twin and subscribe to it. **That subscribe is the migration**: `subscribe` → `restoreSession` → `ensureChatAdopted`, the existing adoption path — provenance check, working-directory recovery, metadata persistence. No adoption logic is duplicated or reimplemented.

- Subscription carries state → adopted; open the agent-host resource.
- Subscription errors → not ours to adopt; open the legacy resource, as today.

Because classification is per-session, it does not depend on the catalogue scan finishing — which is what made list-based gating fragile at scale.

## Impact on other sessions

`migratedCopilotCliResource()` returns `undefined` **synchronously** for anything that is not a `copilotcli:` URI, so native, Claude, and Codex sessions never reach a probe. Already-adopted sessions short-circuit with no round-trip. Probes are bounded (10s) and every failure path degrades to current behaviour.

Failures are deliberately **not** cached: the host reports every restore failure as `SessionNotFound`, so a genuine refusal cannot be told apart from a transient one (host restarting). Caching would silently pin a session to the legacy path for the rest of the window's life.

## List behaviour

The list keeps one rule: if a `copilotcli:` row and its `agent-host-copilotcli:` twin are both present, hide the legacy one. It is a pure function of the current list — no timing, no config, no readiness tracking. A legacy row with no twin stays visible, because opening it now redirects.

Both windows previously carried duplicate copies of this logic; it is now a single shared helper, including the rule that a remote agent-host session
(`remote-<authority>-copilotcli:`) must never be deduped against a local twin even when the raw ids collide.

## Also in this PR

Fixes found while working on the above:

- **Setting off→on no longer loses sessions** — disabling migration retracts adoptable   rows, but discovery skips chats already in the registry and so could never  re-announce them. Re-enabling now restores exactly the retracted keys, and only   forgets a key once it is confirmed surfaced.
- **Working-directory recovery from the extension host's marker**, so worktree sessions   the SDK reports without a `cwd` stay reachable once the extension is retired. The  project resolves from the recovered directory, not the repository root.
- **Discovery is batched**, and a failed marker read is no longer memoized (previously a  session created while the host was running stayed non-adoptable until restart).
- **Discovery retry backs off 250ms/1s/5s** instead of a flat 5s — the race it recovers   from cleared in well under a second in every sampled startup log.

## Testing

- Probe: redirect on adoption, retry after refusal, non-legacy resources never probed,  no connection declines.
- Resource resolution: redirect, no-claim fallback, provider throw falls back rather  than blocking the open.
- Dedupe: twin hides legacy, no twin keeps legacy, remote never deduped, unrelated  providers untouched.
- Host: off→on→off toggle cycle, marker recovery including worktree precedence, and a  marker written after an initial read miss.

title: Fix YAML indentationRules: no indent after property, & typo breaks anchors, missing block-scalar support
body:
Fixes #330394

`extensions/yaml/language-configuration.json` had three separate bugs in its indentation rules, all reported in #330394:

### 1. Typing `foo:` + Enter doesn't indent

`increaseIndentPattern` does match `foo:`, so the regex itself wasn't the problem. The actual cause is in `extensions/yaml/package.json`: a `configurationDefaults` block sets `"editor.autoIndent": "advanced"` for `[yaml]` and `[dockercompose]`, overriding the editor's global default of `"full"`.

`indentationRules` (`increaseIndentPattern`/`decreaseIndentPattern`) are only evaluated when the effective `autoIndent` strategy is `Full` — see the early-return guards in `src/vs/editor/common/languages/autoIndent.ts` (`getInheritIndentForLine`, `getIndentForEnter`, etc.). At `"advanced"`, only `onEnterRules` and the default bracket-pair indent logic run (`src/vs/editor/common/languages/supports/onEnter.ts`), and YAML's language configuration defines no `onEnterRules`. So the increase/decrease-pattern engine was never reached, regardless of whether the pattern matched.

This also explains why the reporter's own extension — registering the identical `language-configuration.json` under a custom language id — worked correctly: it had no matching `configurationDefaults` override, so it inherited the real `"full"` default.

**Fix:** remove the `"editor.autoIndent": "advanced"` override from both `[yaml]` and `[dockercompose]` in `package.json`, letting them fall back to the global `"full"` default. Nothing in the repo's history indicated `"advanced"` was chosen intentionally for these languages.

### 2. Anchors (`foo: &anchor`) don't indent

The pattern used the literal string `&\w+` instead of `&\w+`. This traces back to the commit that introduced `indentationRules` for YAML in 2018 (`1aa00f53bc4`), which appears to have adapted the pattern from a source using HTML/XML entity escaping and never corrected it.

**Fix:** `&` → `&`.

### 3. Block scalars (`foo: |`, `foo: >`) don't indent

`increaseIndentPattern` had no case at all for block scalar indicators. Per the YAML spec, `|` (literal) and `>` (folded) start a block scalar whose content must be indented on following lines, optionally followed by chomping (`-`, `+`) and/or explicit indentation-indicator digits (e.g. `|-`, `>2`, `|+1`).

**Fix:** added `\|[0-9+-]*` and `>[0-9+-]*` as additional alternatives in the pattern's trailing group.

### Testing

Added regression tests in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/codeEditor/test/node/autoindent.test.ts` that load the real `extensions/yaml/language-configuration.json` and verify, via `getReindentEditOperations`, that indentation now increases after a property (`foo:`), an anchor (`foo: &anchor`), and a block scalar (`foo: |`), while a plain scalar (`foo: bar`) correctly does not — guarding against regression.

Full source build compiles cleanly (`npm run compile`, 0 errors) and the existing node unit test suite passes unaffected (14,789 passing; the only 2 failures are pre-existing, unrelated flaky tests in `AgentService` and `McpStdioStateHandler`).

title: Fix Agent Host sandbox configuration ownership

## Summary

- remove Agent Host parsing and propagation of the runtime-managed sandbox enablement value
- always derive the Copilot SDK `sandboxConfig` from Agent Host sandbox settings when the SDK built-in shell is active, allowing the runtime to compose its managed sandbox floor with the host configuration

The Copilot runtime owns managed sandbox policy and composes the effective sandbox floor. title: Notebook Webview scroll distance is improperly reduced
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Yes**

- VS Code Version: `1.129.1`
  - Commit: `8a7abeba6e03ea3af87bfbce9a1b7e48fed567b8`
  - Electron: `42.6.0`
  - Chrome: `148.0.7778.280`
- OS Version: Ubuntu `24.04.4 LTS` (X11), Linux `7.0.0-28-generic`, x64
- Display configuration: GNOME display scale factor `2`; VS Code window zoom level `1`
- Installed notebook-related extensions:
  - `ms-toolsai.jupyter 2025.9.1`
  - `ms-toolsai.jupyter-renderers 1.3.0`

## Summary

In a native Jupyter Notebook, physical mouse-wheel scrolling has a different distance depending on the pointer target:

- Over a code cell, the outer Notebook scroll distance is normal.
- Over a rendered Markdown cell or a regular inline output, the outer Notebook scroll distance is much shorter for the same wheel input.

This is a stable distance/multiplier problem, not a performance problem: there is no visible jank, blocking, or delayed rendering.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a display with a device scale factor greater than 1, open the attached minimal `.ipynb` in VS Code.
2. Ensure the notebook contains a code cell, a rendered Markdown cell, and a code cell with an existing ordinary text output. No kernel execution is required.
3. Place the pointer over the code cell and scroll the physical mouse wheel by one comparable notch. Observe the change in the outer Notebook scroll position.
4. Return to the same starting position. Place the pointer over the rendered Markdown cell and repeat the same wheel input.
5. Repeat step 4 with the pointer over the regular cell output.

## Expected Behaviour

The outer Notebook scroll distance should be consistent for the same physical wheel input, regardless of whether the pointer is over a code cell, rendered Markdown, or a non-scrollable inline output.

## Actual Behaviour

The rendered Markdown and inline output paths scroll a much shorter distance than the code-cell path. The reduction is consistent with an extra division by `window.devicePixelRatio`.

## Investigation / Suspected Root Cause

The Notebook Webview forwards wheel events using `wheelDelta*` values. In the current source, it divides these values by `window.devicePixelRatio` for every Chrome-based runtime:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/view/renderers/webviewPreloads.ts#L676-L694

However, the host-side `StandardWheelEvent` only applies that DPR workaround for Chrome `<= 122`, because Chrome `>= 123` has the upstream fix:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/browser/mouseEvent.ts#L138-L162

On Chrome 148, the two paths therefore differ:

```text
Code cell:
  native wheelDeltaY -> StandardWheelEvent -> wheelDeltaY / 120

Markdown/output Webview:
  native wheelDeltaY -> wheelDeltaY / devicePixelRatio
  -> did-scroll-wheel -> StandardWheelEvent -> wheelDeltaY / devicePixelRatio / 120
```

The code-cell path does not use the Webview forwarding path. Notebook cell editors configure `handleMouseWheel: false`, allowing the native wheel event to reach the Notebook list directly.

The code comments in both places refer to the historical DPR workaround discussed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/146403#issuecomment-1854538928. The host path has since added a Chrome-version gate, while the Notebook Webview path appears not to have added the same gate.

## Possible Fix Direction

Please make the Notebook Webview use the same Chrome-version condition as `StandardWheelEvent`, so DPR normalization is applied only for Chrome `<= 122`, or centralize this normalization to avoid divergent compatibility logic.

## Additional Information

- I found no `editor.mouseWheelScrollSensitivity`, `workbench.list.mouseWheelScrollSensitivity`, or smooth-scrolling override in user or workspace settings.
- Recording: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5da1aa2-9187-4bb4-906d-b5a75f893ab5
- Minimal reproduction notebook: [notebook-scroll-distance-repro.ipynb](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31206697/notebook-scroll-distance-repro.ipynb)
- Developer Tools Console after reproduction: No Notebook/Webview-related errors or warnings were observed in the latest renderer and notebook-rendering logs. The renderer log contains unrelated extension-marketplace network failures, Agent/Chat extension messages, and Node deprecation warnings; those are omitted because they are not triggered by or relevant to this reproduction.
- Latest Insiders result: Not tested. However, the suspected code path has not yet changed upstream.

## Why This Is a New Issue

The following currently open issues were reviewed and are not duplicates:

- `#251347`: large Notebook outputs flicker and later scroll slowly;
- `#203547`: slow scrolling can become stuck at a particular title;
- `#117644`: historical general Notebook scroll performance and jitter;
- `#112134`: a general request to respect the system mouse-scroll-speed setting.

This report is specifically about a deterministic, pointer-target-dependent
wheel-distance mismatch caused by the Webview message path on high-DPI Chrome
runtimes.

title: Select-to-line-start jumps to end of previous line when before an indented token
body:
Fixes #331582

## Problem

When the cursor sits right before an indented token on a line — i.e. right after the leading whitespace/tabs and before the first real character — pressing `Cmd+Shift+Left` (macOS) / `Ctrl+Shift+Home`'s sibling `Shift+Home` (`cursorHomeSelect`) selects backwards across that line's own indentation to column 1, instead of doing anything useful with the previous line:

```ts
const memberships = await this.entityManager.find(
    |CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

Press `Cmd+Shift+Left` once → selection spans only the leading spaces on the *same* line:

```ts
|    CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

Pulling `CompanyMembershipEntity` up onto the `find(` line then requires pressing Backspace once per indentation character/tab-stop, rather than once.

## Root cause

`cursorHomeSelect` and plain `cursorHome` both call the same "smart home" toggle in `MoveOperations.moveToBeginningOfLine` (`src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorMoveOperations.ts`):

- if the cursor isn't yet at the line's first non-whitespace column, move there;
- if it's already there, move to true column 1 of the *same* line.

That second stage never looks outside the current line, so when the cursor is already positioned right before the content (immediately after the indentation), the only thing left to select on that line is the indentation itself — which isn't useful on its own, since a single Backspace from column 1 already joins the line with the previous one and keeps the indentation as-is.

## Fix

In `MoveOperations.moveToBeginningOfLine`, when selecting (`inSelectionMode`) and the cursor is already at the first non-whitespace column of a line that (a) actually has leading whitespace and (b) isn't the first line of the buffer, extend the selection to the end of the previous line instead of column 1 of the current line:

```ts
if (inSelectionMode && firstNonBlankColumn > minColumn && lineNumber > 1) {
    const previousLineNumber = lineNumber - 1;
    return cursor.move(inSelectionMode, previousLineNumber, model.getLineMaxColumn(previousLineNumber), 0);
}
```

A single Backspace afterwards then removes the newline and the entire indentation in one step, pulling the token onto the previous line.

Unaffected on purpose:
- Plain (non-select) `Home`/`Cmd+Left` — unchanged, still stays on the current line.
- Lines with no leading whitespace — nothing to skip, so the toggle behaves as before.
- The first line of the buffer — no previous line to jump to.
- Any selection call where the cursor isn't yet at the first non-whitespace column — unchanged, still moves there first as before.

This only touches the shared model-level move function, so it applies consistently whether reached through the plain (non-wrapped) path or the soft-wrap–aware view-line path that already delegates to it.

## Testing

Added to `src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts`, next to the existing "move to beginning of line" tests:
- The exact repro from the issue (spaces indentation), including that a second press falls back to the normal same-line toggle once there's nothing left to skip.
- Tabs indentation.
- Previous line ending in punctuation (`{`), confirming the cursor lands immediately after it.
- Plain (non-select) Home is unaffected.
- A line with no leading whitespace is unaffected.

Validation performed:
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.js` — 259 passing (254 pre-existing + 5 new), 0 failing.
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursorMoveCommand.test.js` — 56 passing, 0 failing.
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/contrib/wordOperations/test/browser/wordOperations.test.js` — 57 passing, 0 failing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — 0 errors.

title: Agent host: a replayed client tool from a subagent is handled on the parent chat after a restart
body:
### Summary

A client tool that first ran inside a subagent, and is later replayed by the SDK after VS Code restarts, is handled on the parent chat rather than the subagent chat that owns it. It executes and the turn completes, so this is a grouping defect rather than a hang, but the call appears in the wrong conversation and the parent gains a synthesized duplicate.

The in-process half of this is fixed in #330746. This issue is only the after-restart half, which needs coordinated changes and seemed worth raising as one design question rather than patching.

### Why the parent cannot be resolved

The SDK gives the host nothing to resolve it with. The MCP invocation carries only the tool_use id: `extractToolUseId` reads `extra._meta['claudecode/toolUseId']`, and the CLI has the agent id in scope at that dispatch site and deliberately does not include it. The two channels that do carry subagent identity, `canUseTool`'s `agentID` and `parent_tool_use_id` on streamed envelopes, are both unavailable here: a replayed call streams nothing, and inner subagent tools run under `bypassPermissions` so `canUseTool` is skipped.

The host's own inner-to-parent edge (`SubagentRegistry._innerToParent`) is written only by the stream mapper, so it does not exist for a replayed call. `primeFromTranscript` cannot supply it either: it only records `(toolCallId, agentId)` spawn pairs, and it is fed the main transcript, which excludes sidechain entries. Inner calls live in the per-subagent transcripts.

### Why the obvious fix is harmful

Resolving the parent at invoke time, by keeping the registry edge alive past `drainForegroundSpawns` or priming it from elsewhere, is the smaller change and is worse. It sets `parentToolCallId` in cases where the host has no subagent chat, and the signal is then buffered in `_pendingSubagentSignals` awaiting a `subagent_started` that cannot arrive, since that is emitted only from a live inner stream. The parked MCP handler never settles.

The present coupling is safe by accident: the edge exists only when the same code path already emitted `subagent_started`. Any parent resolution from a non-stream source breaks that invariant, which is why #330746 fixes the in-process case with a host-side routing fallback instead.

### What closing the restart case would take

Three coordinated changes, plus one structural wrinkle:

1. **Prime the edge from the SDK's store.** The mapping is persisted as `subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json` -> `toolUseId`, reachable through `listSubagents` and `getSubagentMessages`, whose envelopes carry `parent_tool_use_id`.
2. **Restore a subagent chat for a dangling `Task`.** `_registerRestoredSubagentSummaries` discovers subagents from `ToolResultSubagentContent` gated on `Completed || Running`. The replay case is exactly a `Task` that never completed, which replays as cancelled with no content, so it is skipped.
3. **Populate the routing map.** `_subagentChats` is written only from a live `subagent_started`; no restore path writes it, so routing has nowhere to go even once the chat exists.

The wrinkle: (1) is an async SDK read on a path that is synchronous today.

Shipping only part of this is worse than shipping none. (1) without (2) and (3) is precisely the harmful shape above.

### Offer

I am happy to implement this if it is wanted, and equally happy for it to be closed or reshaped. I have no attachment to the approach above; it is the shape the code suggested to me, not a proposal I am invested in. The reason I am offering rather than just filing is that I want the in-process fix locally today regardless, so the analysis already exists and offering it publicly costs nothing.

If the answer is that client tool execution should be restructured around the SDK invocation instead, as discussed in #330899, this becomes moot and I would rather not build it.

### Environment

Reproduced against a dev container (remote agent host) on `1.133.x`, using the Claude provider.

Related: #330746 (in-process fix), #330899 (root cause of the wider client-tool execution seam).

body:
## Problem

Text typed into the chat input for an Agent Host session can repeatedly disappear, leaving the input reverted to an earlier prefix. In the reported case, the input kept returning to `I want to ` as additional words were typed.

The Agent Host protocol logs show this sequence:

1. `I want to ` was the last server-confirmed `chat/draftChanged` value.
2. The UI remained open and editable after the host considered the backing session explicitly deleted.
3. Each longer draft was sent optimistically through `chat/draftChanged`.
4. The host rejected each action with `Session was explicitly deleted`.
5. Subscription state returned to the last confirmed draft, and that state was reflected back into the live chat input.

As a result, every newly typed suffix disappeared shortly after draft synchronization ran. The same state transition can also occur when reconnect processing replaces optimistic state with a fresh server snapshot.

## Expected

Failure to synchronize a draft should not destroy text currently being edited locally.

## Actual

A protocol rollback or snapshot can be interpreted as an incoming draft update and overwrite the live editor contents. This can make the input appear impossible to type into while the underlying session remains stale or unavailable.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Show a Copilot-icon promo when Chat is collapsed
body:
Adds a dedicated Copilot-icon pip and promo popup for eligible discounted models while Chat is collapsed. Expanded Chat retains the existing input banner. Shared post-update components and model-picker promo behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

69 targeted tests pass at `0a6e1869`, covering configuration bypass, no enrollment for ineligible or hidden surfaces, delayed responses, revocation, existing status-entry behavior, the seen-promo rule, the cold-Chat CTA, and the card vendor icon and its size.

End-to-end proof ran against this branch in a Codespace, driving the real Code OSS window under Xvfb with a real ExP stage per arm. Each row asserts the product's own `tasClientReadTreatmentComplete` cohort event in the Telemetry output channel. Sale response metadata is mocked because no sale is live; assignment, cohort reads and UI are real.

### Treatment — `copilotIconPopup`

Sale arrives against a collapsed Chat: the Copilot pip appears, the promo card opens, and **Try GPT-5.5** opens Chat and selects the promoted model.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/147e1a09-7307-4c22-a4df-eb07a06ceef7

### Control — `none`

Same sale and same collapsed Chat, no pip. Control still emits exactly one cohort event.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65baa6b1-16a0-4469-abf4-f3a0d28bba01

### Already met the sale — no cohort read

The sale is first met as the input banner in an open Chat. After collapsing Chat, the pip never appears, and no cohort is requested at all, because the seen check runs before the ExP read.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66beebee-f689-4f6d-b0e0-267cde93b825

Two defects were found and fixed by this proof:

- A promo shown in Chat now records `chat.seenPromoIds`, so a sale met as a banner never returns as a pip and that user is never assigned a cohort.
- The CTA now waits for a cold Chat to resolve its session before choosing a harness. It previously assumed the local harness, skipped the switch, and left the promoted model unapplied.
- The card shows the model vendor icon again. An earlier slimming pass dropped the provider icon from the card payload and left a generic sparkle.

Tracked as [github/growth-eng#134](https://github.com/github/growth-eng/issues/134).

title: Refactor AgentService instantiation
body:
## Summary

- construct `AgentService` through dependency injection in one strict Agent Host service scope
- expose one `createAgentHostRuntime` composition function that always builds the same complete shared service graph
- build the complete AgentService core and collaborator graph in `agentServiceComposition.ts`; `AgentService` has no service collection, instantiation service, `services.set`, `createInstance`, or service-class construction
- use one guarded initialization bundle for the few genuine callbacks into the fully constructed `AgentService`
- make the only host-specific graph choice explicit: renderer BYOK or unavailable BYOK; quiet mode no longer changes the DI graph
- register the shared authentication service directly for Git state and changeset operations
- replace the test-only AgentService clock callback with `runWithFakedTimers`
- delay Claude SDK environment mutation until the first SDK call so eager graph construction is inert
- keep only entry-point policy—logging, SDK overrides, provider enablement, and transports—in the two main files

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run core-ci`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Agent Host service and provider proxy tests: 405 passing, 17 pending
- strict renderer-BYOK runtime construction test
- standalone agent host startup in quiet/mock and full provider modes
- WebSocket listener probes returned `426 Upgrade Required`

(Written by Copilot)
